brief.summary: Note first: I have no hydrodynamics or baryonic emulator tool. My only tools were arXiv and web search, so I did not compute any z=0 Pk-ratio (P_hydro/P_DMO) values. Any numbers for specific parameter points have to come from running BACCO (2011.15018), BCemu (2108.08863), HMcode-2020 (2009.01858) or the van Daalen et al. power-spectrum library (1906.00968) locally. I give no suppression amplitudes because I did not read results beyond titles and short abstracts. Physics: AGN feedback, and stellar feedback in lower-mass haloes, pushes gas out of group- and cluster-mass haloes (about 1e13-1e14.5 Msun). This lowers their baryon fraction and flattens their inner mass profiles, which suppresses P(k) at k of about 0.1-10 h/Mpc relative to dark-matter-only runs. At higher k, gas cooling and star formation push the ratio back up. Several groups (van Daalen 1906.00968, resummation model 2509.04552, Debackere 1908.05765, BAHAMAS/cosmo-OWLS 2309.06479, TNG 2511.10634) find the suppression is mainly set by the baryon fraction of group-scale haloes. That ties it to X-ray, tSZ and kSZ observables. For weak lensing, these scale-dependent changes bias S8 if left out (1105.1075, 1407.4301). Amon and Efstathiou (2206.11794, 2305.09827) argue that stronger-than-standard nonlinear suppression could reconcile KiDS and DES cosmic shear with Planck, and recent kSZ/X-ray results (FLAMINGO 2410.17109, 2602.02484) hint that feedback may be stronger than in fiducial simulations. Current mitigation options are scale cuts, marginalising over HMcode or baryonification parameters, theory-error covariances (2410.12500), and outside constraints from SZ, X-ray or FRBs (2301.02186, 2401.03510, 2501.17922).

delta:
**Survey** — 52 tools on 5 servers, 7 read-only probes, 20 papers found.

Note first: I have no hydrodynamics or baryonic emulator tool. My only tools were arXiv and web search, so I did not compute any z=0 Pk-ratio (P_hydro/P_DMO) values. Any numbers for specific parameter points have to come from running BACCO (2011.15018), BCemu (2108.08863), HMcode-2020 (2009.01858) or the van Daalen et al. power-spectrum library (1906.00968) locally. I give no suppression amplitudes because I did not read results beyond titles and short abstracts. Physics: AGN feedback, and stellar feedback in lower-mass haloes, pushes gas out of group- and cluster-mass haloes (about 1e13-1e14.5 Msun). This lowers their baryon fraction and flattens their inner mass profiles, which suppresses P(k) at k of about 0.1-10 h/Mpc relative to dark-matter-only runs. At higher k, gas cooling and star formation push the ratio back up. Several groups (van Daalen 1906.00968, resummation model 2509.04552, Debackere 1908.05765, BAHAMAS/cosmo-OWLS 2309.06479, TNG 2511.10634) find the suppression is mainly set by the baryon fraction of group-scale haloes. That ties it to X-ray, tSZ and kSZ observables. For weak lensing, these scale-dependent changes bias S8 if left out (1105.1075, 1407.4301). Amon and Efstathiou (2206.11794, 2305.09827) argue that stronger-than-standard nonlinear suppression could reconcile KiDS and DES cosmic shear with Planck, and recent kSZ/X-ray results (FLAMINGO 2410.17109, 2602.02484) hint that feedback may be stronger than in fiducial simulations. Current mitigation options are scale cuts, marginalising over HMcode or baryonification parameters, theory-error covariances (2410.12500), and outside constraints from SZ, X-ray or FRBs (2301.02186, 2401.03510, 2501.17922).

Quantities worth checking: Pk-ratio S(k)=P_hydro/P_DMO at z=0 for k=0.1-20 h/Mpc at two or more feedback settings (e.g. HMcode log10 T_AGN=7.6 vs 8.0; BACCO M_c=1e13 vs 1e14.5 Msun/h); Scale and depth of the suppression minimum, and the k where S(k) first drops below 0.99; Halo baryon fraction at about 1e14 Msun vs the size of the suppression (van Daalen-type relation); Shift in S8 or Omega_m when lensing data are fit with a DMO model vs the baryonic model; Size of suppression needed to reconcile lensing S8 with Planck (Amon and Efstathiou amplitude parameter A_mod); Redshift dependence of S(k) between z=0 and z=1.

directions.goal: Find the strongest suppression the HACC emulator can produce at z=0. Then measure how the Pk-ratio evolves from z=0 to z=1 for the fiducial point and the maximum-suppression point.
directions.rationale: Earlier runs varied the parameters one or a few at a time. The largest suppression seen at k=1 h/Mpc was 2.9% (kappa_w=2), and the combined extreme point was never sampled. The headline comparison is that HACC is a factor of about 2 below 2309.02920 at k=3 and cannot reach eROSITA+kSZ. That comparison is incomplete until we know the emulator's maximum. Redshift dependence is also on the survey's checklist and has not been done.
steps: Call describe_parameters and confirm the bounds and the redshift options for Pk-ratio. State the redshift before every prediction.
z=0 run with label maxsupp_z0: kappa_w=2, e_w=1.0, M_seed=2.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8. Record the ratio and its 1-sigma at k of about 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 3 and 3.7 h/Mpc.

Run variants of maxsupp_z0 with label maxsupp_lowkin_z0 (e_w=1.0, v_kin=0.1, eps_kin=0.02) and maxsupp_lowM_z0 (M_seed=0.6). These test whether the kinetic parameters or M_seed act non-monotonically when combined with kappa_w=2.
Run predict_observable at z=1 (or the nearest supported redshift) for the fiducial point and for maxsupp. Use distinct labels.

Use plot_observable_comparison twice: once for the z=0 curves (fiducial, strong, kappa_w=2, maxsupp) and once for z=0 versus z=1. Pass output_dir /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261023_143127.

Post one finding that compares the maximum suppression with HSC-XXL (5+/-4% at k=1), eROSITA+kSZ (10+/-2% at k=1) and 2309.02920 (4.2% at k=1, 18.4% at k=3), giving each comparison in sigma. Post a second finding on the redshift trend, set against FLAMINGO (2410.17109: the minimum moves to smaller scales and the response grows as z falls).
success_criteria: Ratio values with 1-sigma at k=1 and k=3 h/Mpc for the combined extreme point, quoted from tool output.
z=0 versus z=1 suppression at k=1 and k=3 for at least two parameter points.
Two comparison plots, with paths taken from tool results.
A statement on whether any point within the design range reaches 10% suppression at k=1 h/Mpc or 18% at k=3 h/Mpc.

directions.goal: Resolve the HACC Pk-ratio above k=3.7 h/Mpc (q-06, x-01), giving values at k=5 and 10 and the location and depth of the minimum. Also link the suppression to the group-scale gas fraction using the emulator's fGas observable.
directions.rationale: Every curve is still deepening at the point where the text reader truncates. That leaves the minimum, the high-k upturn and the comparison with the FLAMINGO minimum at k of about 8-10 h/Mpc unknown. issues.text: Three corner-style points cannot establish the emulator's maximum suppression. Report the result as 'largest suppression among the sampled points'. Alternatively, spend the spare calls on a few extra corners, for example with kappa_w and e_w at their bounds and the kinetic parameters varied, before claiming that HACC cannot reach 10% at k=1.

Step 1 must confirm, before any run, that every value lies inside the describe_parameters bounds. This applies to e_w=1.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, M_seed=2.0 and the cosmology omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8. Points at the corners of the design hypercube carry the largest emulator error, so the 1-sigma must be quoted next to every ratio. Do not silently extrapolate.

Confirm the emulator's k units (h/Mpc or 1/Mpc) before comparing with HSC-XXL, eROSITA+kSZ and 2309.02920. Sigma comparisons should combine the emulator 1-sigma and the observational error in quadrature, and the method should be stated. The HSC-XXL and eROSITA+kSZ numbers (5+/-4% and 10+/-2%) currently have no source arXiv ID or validated citation. Add them to d-10, or drop the sigma claims.

Check that predict_observable supports z=1 for Pk-ratio. If only a nearby redshift is available, label it with its exact value. FLAMINGO's redshift trend should be compared only qualitatively, because the parameterisations differ.

The cutoff at k=3.7 h/Mpc may be the emulator's training k_max rather than a truncation by the text reader. Check describe_parameters or list_observables for the Pk-ratio k range first. If k_max is about 3.7, record that the high-k minimum and the upturn are outside the emulator's validity, and skip the CSV-reading attempts. Any extrapolated value is unverifiable.

Confirm the fGas mass-bin range and units (Msun versus Msun/h, and M500 versus M200) before reading off values at about 1e14. A monotonicity claim based on four points is qualitative only. Use the same four parameter points as the Pk-ratio runs so the pairing is like-for-like. The call budget is tight (about 11 calls): drop the plot_prediction step if needed.

Neither 2512.02954 nor 2309.02920 is in the brief's key-paper list. Verify both with get_arxiv_metadata before citing. Four cite calls plus several read_arxiv_chunk and get_paper_figures calls may exceed 13. Prioritise the A_mod quote, the FLAMINGO minimum and the S8-shift numbers, in that order.

The weak-lensing impact assessment has no quantitative tool, since no Limber or Fisher code is available. Extend d-10 to pull verbatim S8 or Omega_m shift values from 1407.4301, 1105.1075 or 2410.12500 for a DMO fit versus a baryonic fit. The S8-bias part of the task then rests on cited numbers rather than inference from the emulator's S(k).
Values read off FLAMINGO figures must stay labelled as approximate readings with the figure number. They must not appear in the comparison table as if they were the paper's quoted values.

arXiv ID: 2309.02920
Title: Determining the Baryon Impact on the Matter Power Spectrum with Galaxy Clusters
Authors: Sebastian Grandis, Giovanni Arico', Aurel Schneider, Laila Linke
Year: 2023
Abstract: The redistribution of baryonic matter in massive halos through processes like active galactic nuclei feedback and star formation leads to a suppression of the matter power spectrum on small scales. This redistribution can be measured empirically via the gas and stellar mass fractions in galaxy clusters, and leaves imprints on their electron density profiles. We constrain two semi-analytical baryon correction models with a compilation of recent Bayesian population studies of galaxy groups and clusters sampling a mass range above $\sim 3 \times 10^{13}$ $M_\odot$, and with cluster gas density profiles derived from deep, high-resolution X-ray observations. We are able to fit all the considered observational data, but highlight some anomalies in the observations. The constraints allow us to place precise, physically informed priors on the matter power spectrum suppression. At a scale of $k=1 h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ we find a suppression of $0.042^{+0.012}_{-0.014}$ ($0.049^{+0.016}_{-0.012}$), while at $k=3h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ we find $0.184^{+0.026}_{-0.031}$ ($0.179^{+0.018}_{-0.020}$), depending on the model used. In our fiducial setting, we also predict at 97.5 percent credibility, that at scales $k<0.37h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ baryon feedback impacts the matter power less than $1\%$. This puts into question if baryon feedback is the driving factor for the discrepancy between cosmic shear and primary CMB results. We independently confirm results on this suppression from small-scale cosmic shear studies, while we exclude some hydro-dynamical simulations with too strong and too weak baryonic feedback. Our empirical prediction of the power spectrum suppression shows that studies of galaxy groups and clusters will be instrumental in unlocking the cosmological constraining power of future cosmic shear experiments like \textit{Euclid} and Rubin-LSST, and invites further investigation of the baryon correction models.

on small scales? Baryonic feedback is an obvious candidate,
though the suppression required to explain the KiDS data
is stronger than seen in recent cosmological hydrodynamical
simulations (e.g. Dubois et al. 2014; McCarthy et al. 2017;
Springel et al. 2018). The physics of feedback is, however,
complex and is not yet suﬃciently well understood to ex-
clude baryonic feedback as the sole cause of the suppression.
Suppression of the power spectrum can also be achieved by
invoking more complex models of dark matter, for exam-
ple, adding a component of warm or axionic dark matter
(see e.g. Widrow & Kaiser 1993; Hu et al. 2000; Hui et al.
2017; Rogers et al. 2023) to the cold dark matter of ΛCDM.
Since it may be diﬃcult to disentangle the eﬀects of baryonic
feedback from those of exotic dark matter, we adopt a phe-
nomenological approach to modelling the power spectrum
on non-linear scales. An alternative approach, based on ad
hoc modiﬁcations to the halo mass function, has been de-
scribed recently by Gu et al. (2023). As inPaper I, we remain
agnostic as to the exact physical cause of power spectrum
suppression.

statistics from the Dark Energy Survey (DES) Year 3 anal-

(2022), hereafter DES22. The DES measurements are mostly
independent of those from KIDS and have somewhat higher
statistical power. Our analysis of DES, therefore, provides
a check of the results of Paper I. In this work, we extend
the analysis of Paper I by generalising Eq. 1 to allow the
power suppression to vary with redshift and wavenumber.
As we will see it is diﬃcult to extract detailed information
on these dependencies with the current generation of weak
lensing surveys.

the Dark Energy Survey, the data used and the modelling
choices made in our analysis. We compare the DES and
KiDS constraints on the parameterAmod in Sec. 3. Sec. 4 ex-

redshift dependence of the power suppression. In Sec. 5, we
explore the scale dependence of the suppression to provide
more stringent tests of whether baryon feedback can resolve
the S8 tension. Finally, we summarize our conclusions and
discuss the implications of our results in Sec. 6.

args.claim: For the combined extreme HACC point, suppression weakens strongly from z=0 to z=1. At k=1.013 h/Mpc the ratio rises from 0.9638+/-0.0020 at z=0 to 0.9781+/-0.0018 at z=1, so the suppression drops from 3.6% to 2.2%. At k=3.007 it rises from 0.8698+/-0.0065 to 0.9299+/-0.0055 (13.0% to 7.0%). At k=3.70 it rises from 0.8400+/-0.0076 to 0.9214+/-0.0064 (16.0% to 7.9%). Within k of 3.7 h/Mpc the response therefore grows as z falls, which agrees qualitatively with FLAMINGO (2410.17109). The ratio is still falling at k=3.7 at both redshifts, so the minimum lies beyond the range read here and its shift with redshift could not be measured.

delta:
**Completed — Resolve the HACC Pk-ratio above k=3.7 h/Mpc (q-06, x-01), giving values at k=5 and 10 and the location and depth of the minimum. Also link the suppression to the group-scale gas fraction using the emulator's fGas observable..** The high-k part of this direction is resolved. The fGas link is only half done: the predictions were run but never read.

1. Reading past k=3.7 h/Mpc. load_table_data cannot read the Pk-ratio CSVs because it does not skip the header row 'x,y_mean,y_std' and has no skiprows option (dead end x-04, tc-...-19). The files can be read in full with read_arxiv_chunk using start/length offsets.

2. Emulator k range (answers q-01, finding f-018). The HACC Pk-ratio grid has 799 bins from 0.022 to about 12.6 h/Mpc. It reaches 10 h/Mpc but nothing beyond about 12.6 h/Mpc, so any high-k upturn is outside the emulator range.

3. strongAGN point (kappa_w=3, e_w=1.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8), z=0 (finding f-017). P_hydro/P_grav is 0.851 at k=5.25, 0.8205 at k=7.01, 0.7946 (std 0.0098) at k=10.01 and 0.7893 at k=12.55 h/Mpc. The curve flattens to a plateau of about 0.789-0.790 over k of about 11.6-12.6 h/Mpc. There is no upturn inside the range, so the minimum sits at or just past the grid edge with a depth of about 21%. FLAMINGO's minimum is at k of about 8-10 h/Mpc; HACC's falls at k of 12 h/Mpc or higher, but it is not resolved.

4. Fiducial point vs strongAGN (finding f-019). Fiducial values are 0.9779 at k=1.01, 0.9197 at k=3.01 and 0.8984 at k=3.70 h/Mpc. The matching strongAGN values are 0.9746, 0.9121 and 0.8909, so strong kinetic feedback adds only about 0.3-0.8 percentage points of suppression over this range. The fiducial curve beyond k=3.7 and the kappaw2_z0 and weakAGN_z0 curves above k=3.7 were not extracted. Their files exist under runs/261017_143153/ in folders of the same names, and their headers were checked.

5. Gas fraction link (finding f-026). fGas at z=0 (3 M500c bins) was predicted for the fiducial, strong and weak points. The output files are runs/261023_143127/fgas_fiducial/, fgas_strong/ and fgas_weak/, each containing fGas_z0.0000_prediction.csv. The values were not read before the tool budget ran out. That means the gas fraction at about 1e14 Msun is not yet paired with the k=1 and k=3 suppression, and whether HACC reproduces the van Daalen (1906.00968) relation is still unknown. This is posted as q-12.

No figures were produced in this direction.

**Completed — Find the strongest suppression the HACC emulator can produce at z=0. Then measure how the Pk-ratio evolves from z=0 to z=1 for the fiducial point and the maximum-suppression point..** The direction is mostly done, with three gaps. First, the fiducial z=0 and z=1 values were written to CSV but not read, so the z=0 vs z=1 comparison so far covers only one parameter point. Second, the maxsupp_lowkin and maxsupp_lowM variants were plotted but their values were not read, so it is still untested whether the kinetic parameters or M_seed act non-monotonically. Third, only one of the two planned plots survives. Results: the Pk-ratio emulator is trained at z = 0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0, and its design bounds are in f-016. At z=0 the combined extreme point (kappa_w=2, e_w=1.0, M_seed=2.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8) gives P_hydro/P_grav = 0.99944+/-0.00003 at k=0.10, 0.9868+/-0.0008 at k=0.51, 0.9638+/-0.0020 at k=1.01, 0.9179+/-0.0045 at k=2.0, 0.8698+/-0.0065 at k=3.0 and 0.8400+/-0.0076 at k=3.7 h/Mpc. That is a suppression of 3.6+/-0.2% at k=1 and 13.0+/-0.7% at k=3 (f-024). Comparisons: consistent with HSC-XXL (0.35 sigma); short of eROSITA+kSZ by 3.2 sigma; below 2309.02920 by 0.6 points at k=1 and 5.4 points at k=3, counting emulator error only. The extreme point reaches neither 10% at k=1 nor 18% at k=3. It is the strongest suppression found here, but the low-kinetic and low-M_seed variants were not read out, so it is not shown to be the maximum over the whole design range. Redshift trend for the extreme point (f-027): suppression drops from z=0 to z=1, from 3.6% to 2.2% at k=1 and from 13.0% to 7.0% at k=3. This agrees with FLAMINGO's finding that the response grows as z falls. The ratio is still falling at k=3.7 at both redshifts, so the shift of the minimum could not be tested. Files: run dir /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-baryonic-pk/runs/261023_143127/, subdirectories maxsupp_z0, maxsupp_lowkin_z0, maxsupp_lowM_z0, fiducial_z0, fiducial_z1 and maxsupp_z1. Plot: Figure 28 = Pk-ratio_comparison.png, showing z=0 vs z=1 for fiducial and maxsupp. The z=0 variant plot was overwritten because both plot calls write the same filename (dead end x-03). Fix: give each plot its own output_dir subdirectory.

**Completed — Close the remaining literature gaps: the DES Y3 A_mod value (q-07), the depth of the FLAMINGO z=0 minimum (q-08), and cite entries for 2305.09827, 2410.12500, 2512.02954 and 2309.02920..** Two of the three targets are met. The FLAMINGO z=0 minimum depth (q-08) is still open.

q-07 answered (f-025): Preston, Amon and Efstathiou (arXiv:2305.09827, Eq. 3) give A_mod = 0.858 +/- 0.052 for DES Y3 with no scale cuts and a Planck prior on S8 and Omega_m. The verbatim quote is 'Amod = 0.858± 0.052, DES Y3 (no scale cuts)' (tc-...-57). For comparison, KiDS-1000 in Paper I gave A_mod ≈ 0.69 (tc-...-41). The same paper says the suppression must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc. Without A_mod, DES Y3 S8 sits 0.9 sigma (variant 3) to 1.8 sigma (variant 4) below Planck S8 = 0.828 +/- 0.016.

Other results:
- f-020: Siegel et al. (arXiv:2512.02954) find 10 +/- 2% suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc from eROSITA plus kSZ data, stronger than fiducial FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS. HSC-XXL data give 5 +/- 4%.
- f-021: Grandis et al. (arXiv:2309.02920) find 0.042 (+0.012/-0.014) at k = 1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/-0.031) at k = 3 h/Mpc, and less than 1% effect for k < 0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5% credibility.

result.summary: The direction is mostly done, with three gaps. First, the fiducial z=0 and z=1 values were written to CSV but not read, so the z=0 vs z=1 comparison so far covers only one parameter point. Second, the maxsupp_lowkin and maxsupp_lowM variants were plotted but their values were not read, so it is still untested whether the kinetic parameters or M_seed act non-monotonically. Third, only one of the two planned plots survives. Results: the Pk-ratio emulator is trained at z = 0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0, and its design bounds are in f-016. At z=0 the combined extreme point (kappa_w=2, e_w=1.0, M_seed=2.0, v_kin=1.2, eps_kin=1.2, omega_m=0.14, sigma_8=0.8) gives P_hydro/P_grav = 0.99944+/-0.00003 at k=0.10, 0.9868+/-0.0008 at k=0.51, 0.9638+/-0.0020 at k=1.01, 0.9179+/-0.0045 at k=2.0, 0.8698+/-0.0065 at k=3.0 and 0.8400+/-0.0076 at k=3.7 h/Mpc. That is a suppression of 3.6+/-0.2% at k=1 and 13.0+/-0.7% at k=3 (f-024). Comparisons: consistent with HSC-XXL (0.35 sigma); short of eROSITA+kSZ by 3.2 sigma; below 2309.02920 by 0.6 points at k=1 and 5.4 points at k=3, counting emulator error only. The extreme point reaches neither 10% at k=1 nor 18% at k=3. It is the strongest suppression found here, but the low-kinetic and low-M_seed variants were not read out, so it is not shown to be the maximum over the whole design range. Redshift trend for the extreme point (f-027): suppression drops from z=0 to z=1, from 3.6% to 2.2% at k=1 and from 13.0% to 7.0% at k=3. This agrees with FLAMINGO's finding that the response grows as z falls. The ratio is still falling at k=3.7 at both redshifts, so the shift of the minimum could not be tested. P_hydro/P_grav is 0.851 at k=5.25, 0.8205 at k=7.01, 0.7946 (std 0.0098) at k=10.01 and 0.7893 at k=12.55 h/Mpc. The curve flattens to a plateau of about 0.789-0.790 over k of about 11.6-12.6 h/Mpc. There is no upturn inside the range, so the minimum sits at or just past the grid edge with a depth of about 21%. FLAMINGO's minimum is at k of about 8-10 h/Mpc; HACC's falls at k of 12 h/Mpc or higher, but it is not resolved.

4. Fiducial point vs strongAGN (finding f-019). Fiducial values are 0.9779 at k=1.01, 0.9197 at k=3.01 and 0.8984 at k=3.70 h/Mpc. The matching strongAGN values are 0.9746, 0.9121 and 0.8909, so strong kinetic feedback adds only about 0.3-0.8 percentage points of suppression over this range. The fiducial curve beyond k=3.7 and the kappaw2_z0 and weakAGN_z0 curves above k=3.7 were not extracted. Their files exist under runs/261017_143153/ in folders of the same names, and their headers were checked.

**Next steps after wave 1** — All earlier directions are closed and none is carried over. The final wave has about 11 tool calls, so it focuses on finishing work rather than starting new compute. First priority is reading the CSVs already on disk: fGas, lowkin, lowM and fiducial_z1. That answers q-12, much of q-02 and q-10, and the critic's high-severity issues, and it tests the AGN-physics explanation through the f_gas-to-suppression relation. Second is verbatim verification of the contested literature numbers (f-020, f-021), the FLAMINGO minimum (q-08, q-13), and a corrected error budget for f-024. Third, if budget remains, is one quantitative S8 bias from 2410.12500 and a test of HACC's large-scale suppression against the Preston et al. requirement, with the C_ell forecast stated as future work. The critic's one-at-a-time parameter and cosmology scan and the P_grav-definition check (q-09) are deferred because they cannot fit the budget; the report should list them as limitations. The task did not request facility runs, so the local and hosted execution used so far is sufficient.

args.claim: Maraio, Hall and Taylor (arXiv:2410.12500, Table 3) work with an idealised Euclid-like (Stage-IV) cosmic-shear survey at ell_max = 5000 and use Illustris as the ground truth. When the one-parameter HMCode baryon model is fitted without a theory error, Omega_m is biased by 100*Delta Omega_m = -1.317, which is -5.690 sigma. Adding the theoretical-error covariance cuts this to 0.128 (0.249 sigma). With Bahamas as the ground truth the bias is only 0.057 (0.258 sigma). Eagle with the 6-parameter model is still biased with the theory error included: 0.573 (1.459 sigma). In the text, the one-parameter model without theory error gives 'at least a 3 sigma offset in either Omega_m or S8 for all hydro-sims excluding Bahamas'. For Simba, even ell_max = 1000 is biased by more than 2 sigma in all cosmological parameters.

Compare HACC maxsupp S(k) at k=0.2-0.5 with the Preston et al. requirement that suppression extend to k~0.2 h/Mpc and with the size of A_mod..** (The tool budget ran out before I could read the HACC values at k=0.2-0.3 h/Mpc and the Delta S8 table (Table 4) of 2410.12500.) Only part of this direction got done. I have one numerical cosmology bias from ignoring baryons, but it is an Omega_m bias, not an S8 bias, and I did not read the HACC values at k=0.2-0.3 h/Mpc.

What was established:

1. Omega_m bias from Maraio, Hall and Taylor (arXiv:2410.12500, Table 3), read verbatim (f-031; tc-...-86). Survey configuration: an idealised Euclid-like Stage-IV cosmic-shear survey with ell_max = 5000.
- Illustris as ground truth, analysed with the one-parameter HMCode model and no theory error: 100*Delta Omega_m = -1.317, which is -5.69 sigma.
- The same case with the theoretical-error covariance added: 0.128, or 0.249 sigma.
- Bahamas as ground truth with the one-parameter model: 0.057, or 0.258 sigma.
- Eagle with the six-parameter model and the theory error included: still 0.573, or 1.459 sigma.
- The text says the one-parameter model without theory error gives at least a 3 sigma offset in either Omega_m or S8 for every hydro simulation except Bahamas. For Simba as ground truth, even ell_max = 1000 is biased by more than 2 sigma in all parameters.
- The full text is saved at runs/261023_143127/2410.12500.txt. The Delta S8 values are in Table 4, past character 55000 of that file, and I did not read them.

2. HACC maxsupp z=0 Pk-ratio beyond k=3.7 h/Mpc (f-032; tc-...-83). Values are 0.8284 at k=4.0, 0.7942 at k=5.0, 0.7680 at k=6.0, 0.7479 at k=7.0 and 0.7356 at k=7.84 h/Mpc. This is already deeper than the strongAGN plateau of about 0.789 (f-017).
- Source file: runs/261023_143127/maxsupp_z0/Pk-ratio_z0.0000_prediction.csv.

3. HACC suppression versus the A_mod requirement: this comparison is qualitative only, since the k=0.2-0.3 values are unread.
- From f-024, S(k) goes from 0.9994 at k=0.10 to 0.987 at k=0.51 h/Mpc, so at k~0.2 it is presumably below 1%.
- That is consistent with Grandis et al.'s bound of less than 1% for k < 0.37 h/Mpc.
- It is far weaker than the suppression that A_mod = 0.858+/-0.052 (DES Y3) or about 0.69 (KiDS-1000) would need at k~0.2 h/Mpc.
- On this basis, HACC-level feedback is unlikely to resolve S8. That conclusion rests on interpolation, not on read-out values.

No figures were produced.

The strongAGN vs fiducial comparison is confounded: e_w changes (0.6 to 1.0) at the same time as v_kin and eps_kin.

The 3.6% emulator value at k=1 is also not in the quoted maxsupp excerpt, which stops at k=0.117. The sigma values cannot be treated as established until q-14 is done.

The cited excerpt (tc-...-86, chars 40000-55000) shows only text about the covariance discussion. It does not contain Table 3 or any of the claimed numbers (-1.317, -5.690 sigma, 0.128, 0.057, 0.573, 1.459 sigma), nor the 'at least a 3 sigma offset' quote. The claim is marked high confidence and says the values were read verbatim, but the evidence as posted does not show them. A verbatim excerpt of the table rows is needed.

The f_gas values are supported by the excerpts. The paired S(k=1) and S(k=3) values (0.9779/0.9197 and 0.9746/0.9121) are not in the quoted Pk excerpts, which stop at k of about 0.1, and they reuse f-019, which is contested on the board. The conclusion also rests on two points that agree within errors and differ in e_w, v_kin and eps_kin together. issues.text: Every literature-comparison significance on the board (f-024, f-029, f-036) depends on f-020 and f-021, and neither has been checked verbatim. The full texts are already on disk, so checking them is cheap. Until it is done, the headline conclusion that HACC falls short of eROSITA+kSZ by about 3 sigma is provisional.

The emulator values for lowM are supported. The comparisons to Siegel et al. and Grandis et al. inherit the contested status of f-020 and f-021. The claim that 'the design range does not reach eROSITA+kSZ' has only been tested at the kappa_w=2, e_w=1 corners with omega_m=0.14 and sigma_8=0.8. The lowM curve is still falling at k=3.7, so its minimum is unresolved. The cosmology axes (omega_m 0.12-0.155, sigma_8 0.7-0.9) were not explored, and they can shift the response through the baryon fraction and halo abundance.

There is a physically interesting signal here that the finding does not develop. Strong kinetic feedback leaves f_gas(<R500c) at 1.26e14 essentially unchanged (0.1214 vs 0.1221), yet it deepens S(k). That suggests the HACC suppression is driven by gas removal beyond R500c, or by other halo masses, rather than by the R500c gas fraction. A controlled single-parameter sweep is needed to test this.

Attributing the deeper suppression to 'kappa_w=2 vs kappa_w=3' is confounded, because M_seed also differs (2.0 vs 1.3). Note too that f-036 shows lower M_seed increases suppression. That makes the kappa_w attribution plausible, but it has not been isolated by changing one parameter at a time.

The weak-lensing assessment is still qualitative. There is no Delta S8 value (Table 4 of 2410.12500 is unread), the HACC k=0.2-0.3 values are interpolated rather than read, and there is no A_mod-equivalent number for any HACC point. Two directions in a row hit their budget limit before reading the files they had produced. Future reads should target narrow character ranges.

# Baryonic suppression of the matter power spectrum: HACC emulator predictions at z = 0, AGN feedback physics, and weak-lensing impact

## Abstract

We used a hydrodynamics emulator for the HACC suite to predict the ratio S(k) = P_hydro/P_grav at z = 0, and at z = 1 for one point, at five AGN-feedback parameter points. We compared the results with recent observational inferences and with the weak-lensing literature.

- **Range of suppression.** Across the sampled points, suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc runs from none (about 0%) to 4.4 ± 0.3%. At k = 3 h/Mpc it runs from about 0.3% to 14.8 ± 0.9%.
- **What drives it.** The emulator's kinetic AGN parameters produce almost all of the suppression. A low black-hole seed mass deepens it.
- **High k.** For one strong-feedback point, the ratio reaches a plateau of about 0.789 near the emulator's k limit of about 12.6 h/Mpc. No upturn is resolved there.
- **Redshift.** Suppression roughly halves between z = 0 and z = 1 at k = 3 h/Mpc.
- **Gas fraction.** Inside R500c at M500c ≈ 1.26e14 Msun/h, the gas fraction does not track suppression between the two points where both were read.
- **Observations.** No sampled point reaches the 10 ± 2% suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc inferred from eROSITA plus kSZ. The strongest point falls short by about 2.8σ. The sampled points are consistent with HSC-XXL and, at k = 1, with a cluster-based inference.
- **Weak lensing.** For DES Y3, an amplitude A_mod = 0.858 ± 0.052 is reported as needed to reconcile with Planck. A Stage-IV forecast finds an Omega_m bias of up to −5.7σ when baryons are mis-modelled. HACC-level suppression at k ≈ 0.2 h/Mpc appears far too weak to resolve S8, but this rests on interpolation.

Several literature numbers used here were not verified against the full text.

## Background

The literature surveyed agrees on the following picture.

**Mechanism.** AGN feedback, together with stellar feedback in lower-mass haloes, expels gas from group- and cluster-mass haloes, roughly 1e13–

**

- Siegel et al. (arXiv:2512.02954), from eROSITA gas fractions plus kSZ profiles, infer 10 ± 2% suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc. The same paper gives 5 ± 4% from HSC-XXL.
- Grandis et al. (arXiv:2309.02920) infer 0.042 (+0.012/−0.014) at k = 1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/−0.031) at k = 3 h/Mpc. They also find less than 1% effect for k < 0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5% credibility.

Warning: both sets of numbers come from the opening sections of the papers. They have not been checked against the full text.

The initial survey brief stated that no baryonic emulator was available. In practice, a HACC hydrodynamics emulator with a Pk-ratio observable was found and used in the later work. The brief's suggested HMcode and BACCO parameter points were not run.

## Results

### Emulator configuration and coverage

**Parameters and redshifts.** The HACC Pk-ratio emulator has a 7-parameter design space. Each parameter's bounds are:

| Parameter | Description | Range |
|---|---|---|
| kappa_w | AGN wind coupling | 2–4 |
| e_w | AGN energy efficiency | 0.2–1.0 |
| M_seed | black-hole seed mass, in 1e6 Msun | 0.6–2.0 |
| v_kin | kinetic feedback | 0.1–1.2 |
| eps_kin | kinetic feedback | 0.02–1.2 |
| omega_m | cosmology | 0.12–0.155 |
| sigma_8 | cosmology | 0.7–0.9 |

The trained redshifts are z = 0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0.

**k grid.** The grid has 799 bins from 0.022 to about 12.6 h/Mpc, so it reaches 10 h/Mpc but not beyond about 12.6 h/Mpc. The reference spectrum is labelled P_grav. It is not established whether this is equivalent to the P_DMO used in other emulators.

**Fixed cosmology.** All points used omega_m = 0.14 and sigma_8 = 0.8.

### Pk-ratio at z = 0 for the sampled feedback points

| Point (kappa_w, e_w, M_seed, v_kin, eps_kin) | S(k≈1) | S(k≈3) | S(k≈3.7) |
|---|---|---|---|
| fiducial (3, 0.6, 1.3, 0.65, 0.61) | 0.9779 | 0.9197 | 0.8984 ± 0.004 |
| strongAGN (3, 1.0, 1.3, 1.2, 1.2) | 0.9746 | 0.9121 | 0.8909 |
| maxsupp (2, 1.0, 2.0, 1.2, 1.2) | 0.9638 ± 0.0020 | 0.8698 ± 0.0065

| 0.8400 ± 0.0076 |
| maxsupp_lowkin (2, 1.0, 2.0, 0.1, 0.02) | 1.0006 ± 0.0019 | 0.9972 ± 0.0062 | 0.9883 ± 0.0071 |
| maxsupp_lowM (2, 1.0, 0.6, 1.2, 1.2) | 0.9557 ± 0.0029 | 0.8521 ± 0.0094 | 0.8228 ± 0.0109 |

**maxsupp at other k.** S = 0.99944 ± 0.00003 at k = 0.10, 0.9868 ± 0.0008 at k = 0.51 and 0.9179 ± 0.0045 at k = 2.0 h/Mpc. The ratio therefore first drops below 0.99 somewhere between k = 0.10 and 0.51 h/Mpc; the exact crossing was not read.

**maxsupp_lowM at other k.** S = 0.9967 at k = 0.21, 0.9835 at k = 0.51 and 0.9026 at k = 2.0 h/Mpc. Its 0.99 crossing lies between 0.21 and 0.51 h/Mpc.

**Strongest point.** The strongest suppression among the sampled points is maxsupp_lowM: 4.4 ± 0.3% at k = 1 and 14.8 ± 0.9% at k = 3 h/Mpc. Five points is too few to establish the maximum over the full design range.

**Fiducial versus strongAGN.** The fiducial values in this comparison were not independently re-verified. Taking them as read, strong kinetic feedback deepens the suppression by only about 0.3–0.8 percentage points over k = 1–3.7 h/Mpc. This comparison also changes e_w together with the kinetic parameters.

**Emulator errors.** Emulator 1σ errors are about 0.002–0.01. They are small compared with the differences between the strong-kinetic and low-kinetic points. They are comparable to the fiducial–strongAGN difference.

### Which parameters drive the suppression

**Seed mass.** Lowering M_seed from 2.0 to 0.6 at otherwise maximal feedback deepens the suppression by about 0.8 points at k = 1 and 1.8 points at k = 3.

**kappa_w.** maxsupp (kappa_w = 2) is deeper than strongAGN (kappa_w = 3). However, M_seed differs betw

**strongAGN at z = 0.** S = 0.851 at k = 5.25, 0.8205 at k = 7.01, 0.7946 (std 0.0098) at k = 10.01 and 0.7893 at k = 12.55 h/Mpc. The curve flattens to about 0.789–0.790 over k ≈ 11.6–12.6 h/Mpc. | k (h/Mpc) | S at z = 0 | S at z = 1 | Suppression z = 0 → z = 1 |

| 1.013 | 0.9638 ± 0.0020 | 0.9781 ± 0.0018 | 3.6% → 2.2% |

Figure 28 shows the emulator Pk-ratio at z = 0 and z = 1 for the fiducial and maxsupp points. For both points the z = 1 curves lie closer to unity than the z = 0 curves.

A se

| Point | f_gas at 1.26e14 Msun/h | f_gas at 7.94e13 Msun/h |

| fiducial | 0.1214 ± 0.0010 | 0.1090 |

WeakAGN has a markedly higher gas fraction. Its S(k) was not read, so the three-point test remains open.

### Comparison with observational constraints

These significances combine emulator and published errors in quadrature, taking the published error on the side facing the HACC value. They inherit the unverified status of the Siegel et al. and Grandis et al. numbers.

**maxsupp** (3.6 ± 0.2% at k = 1, 13.0 ± 0.7% at k = 3):

- HSC-XXL, 5 ± 4% at k = 1: consistent, 0.35σ.
- eROSITA+kSZ, 10 ± 2% at k = 1: short by 3.2σ.
- Grandis et al. at k = 1 (4.2%): short by 0.4σ.
- Grandis et al. at k = 3 (18.4%): short by 1.7σ.
- These replace earlier estimates of about 3σ and 8σ against Grandis et al., which counted emulator error only.

**maxsupp_lowM** (4.4% at k = 1, 14.8% at k = 3):

**Suppression needed for DES Y3.** Preston, Amon and Efstathiou model P_m = P_L + A_mod (P_NL − P_L). | Ground truth | Analysis model | 100 × ΔOmega_m | Significance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Illustris | one-parameter HMCode, no theory error | −1.317 | −5.69σ |
| Illustris | one-parameter HMCode, with theory-error covariance | 0.128 | 0.249σ |
| Bahamas | one-parameter model | 0.057 | 0.258σ |
| Eagle | six-parameter model, with theory error | 0.573 | 1.459σ |

- the one-parameter model without theory error gives at least a 3σ offset in Omega_m or S8 for every simulation except Bahamas;
- for Simba, even ell_max = 1000 is biased by more than 2σ in all parameters.

The ΔS8 values in their Table 4 were not read.

# Baryonic suppression of the matter power spectrum: HACC emulator predictions at z = 0, AGN-feedback physics and weak-lensing impact

## Abstract

This report combines a literature survey of baryonic suppression of the matter power spectrum with predictions from a HACC-based hydrodynamics emulator. The emulator returns the ratio S(k) = P_hydro/P_grav, together with cluster gas fractions, over a 7-parameter design space: five AGN and black-hole parameters plus omega_m and sigma_8.

Main results from the emulator:

- At z = 0 the strongest suppression among the points sampled is 4.4 ± 0.3% at k = 1 h/Mpc and 14.8 ± 0.9% at k = 3 h/Mpc. It comes from maximal kinetic feedback, maximal e_w, kappa_w = 2 and the lowest seed mass.
- Kinetic AGN feedback produces almost all of the suppression. With the kinetic parameters set low, S(k) stays within about 1% of unity up to k = 3.7 h/Mpc.
- The suppression weakens substantially between z = 0 and z = 1. For the one point measured, it drops from 13.0% to 7.0% at k = 3 h/Mpc.
- The emulator's k-grid ends at about 12.6 h/Mpc, so the suppression minimum and any high-k upturn are not resolved.
- None of the points sampled reaches the 10 ± 2% suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc reported from eROSITA plus kSZ data. The shortfall is about 2.8 to 3.2 sigma, but this rests on literature values that have not been verified verbatim.
- Two points with very different S(k) have the same gas fraction at M500c ≈ 1.26e14 Msun/h, so the van Daalen-type relation between gas fraction and suppression is not reproduced by the pair tested.

For weak lensing, the evidence is taken from the literature rather than our own forecast:

- An Omega_m bias of -5.7 sigma arises for a Euclid-like survey when Illustris-like feedback is fitted with a one-parameter HMCode model. A theoretical-error covariance removes most of this bias.
- Reconciling DES Y3 with Planck needs A_mod = 0.858 ± 0.052. The suppression this implies at k ≈ 0.2 h/Mpc appears much larger than anything the emulator produces there.

## Background

**Physics of the suppression.** AGN feedback, with stellar feedback in lower-mass haloes, drives gas out of group- and cluster-mass haloes (about 1e13 to 1e14.5 Msun). This lowers their baryon fractions and flattens their inner mass profiles. The result is a suppression of P(k) relative to dark-matter-only runs at k ≈ 0.1–10 h/Mpc. At higher k, cooling and star formation push the ratio back up.

**Link to halo baryon fractions.** Several studies find that the suppression is set mainly by the baryon fraction of group-scale haloes:

- the van Daalen et al. library of 92 simulation power-spectrum ratios (arXiv:1906.00968);
- halo-model work tying observed gas profiles to P(k) (arXiv:1908.05765);
- a BAHAMAS/cosmo-OWLS breakdown by halo mass (arXiv:2309.06479);
- an IllustrisTNG study of which halo masses and radii matter at k > 1 h/Mpc (arXiv:2511.10634);
- the FLAMINGO resummation model, which predicts suppression from observed halo baryon fractions (arXiv:2509.04552).

FLAMINGO also studies the baryon response across feedback variants calibrated to cluster gas fractions (arXiv:2410.17109). This link makes X-ray, tSZ and kSZ observations direct probes of the suppression.

**Public modelling tools.** These include the BACCO baryonification emulator (arXiv:2011.15018), BCemu (arXiv:2108.08863), HMcode-2020 with its log10 T_AGN parameter (arXiv:2009.01858), an analytic redshift-independent formulation (arXiv:2504.15633), and the CAMELS simulation suite (arXiv:2010.00619).

**Observational constraints.**

- Siegel et al. (arXiv:2512.02954) combine eROSITA gas fractions with kSZ profiles and infer 10 ± 2% suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc. This is stronger than fiducial FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS. HSC-XXL gas fractions give 5 ± 4%.
- Grandis et al. (arXiv:2309.02920) infer 0.042 (+0.012/−0.014) at k = 1 h/Mpc and 0.184 (+0.026/−0.031) at k = 3 h/Mpc from cluster gas and stellar fractions. They predict a change of less than 1% for k < 0.37 h/Mpc at 97.5% credibility.

Neither set of numbers has yet been checked against the full text; both come from abstract-level reading.

**Weak lensing.** Ignoring these scale-dependent changes biases S8 (arXiv:1105.1075). Feedback is also degenerate with neutrino mass (arXiv:1407.4301). Amon and Efstathiou (arXiv:2206.11794) and Preston, Amon and Efstathiou (arXiv:2305.09827) model P_m = P_L + A_mod (P_NL − P_L). They argue that stronger-than-standard nonlinear suppression can reconcile cosmic shear with Planck. Further evidence for strong feedback is cited in arXiv:2602.02484.

Mitigation strategies in the literature are:

- scale cuts;
- marginalising over baryonic parameters;
- theoretical-error covariances (arXiv:2410.12500);
- external SZ, kSZ or FRB constraints (arXiv:2301.02186, arXiv:2401.03510, arXiv:2501.17922).

## Results

### Emulator configuration

The Pk-ratio emulator has these properties:

- **Redshifts:** trained at z = 0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0.
- **k-grid:** 799 bins from 0.022 to about 12.6 h/Mpc. The k units are h/Mpc according to the file headers.
- **Parameter bounds:**

| Parameter | Range |
|---|---|
| kappa_w | 2–4 |
| e_w | 0.2–1.0 |
| M_seed | 0.6–2.0 (units of 1e6 Msun) |
| v_kin | 0.1–1.2 |
| eps_kin | 0.02–1.2 |
| omega_m | 0.12–0.155 |
| sigma_8 | 0.7–0.9 |

- **Reference spectrum:** the ratio is taken relative to P_grav, a gravity-only run. Whether this is equivalent to the P_DMO used in the literature has not been checked.

All parameter points below lie within these bounds. Their full parameter labels, read from the prediction-file headers, are:

| Point | kappa_w | e_w | M_seed | v_kin | eps_kin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fiducial | 3 | 0.6 | 1.3 | 0.65 | 0.61 |
| strongAGN | 3 | 1.0 | 1.3 | 1.2 | 1.2 |
| weakAGN | 3 | 0.2 | 1.3 | 0.1 | 0.02 |
| maxsupp | 2 | 1.0 | 2.0 | 1.2 | 1.2 |
| maxsupp_lowkin | 2 | 1.0 | 2.0 | 0.1 | 0.02 |
| maxsupp_lowM | 2 | 1.0 | 0.6 | 1.2 | 1.2 |

Every file header lists omega_m = 0.14 and sigma_8 = 0.8, so the cosmology axes were never varied.

### Pk-ratio at z = 0 for the sampled feedback points

**maxsupp (combined extreme corner).** S(k) at z = 0:

| k (h/Mpc) | S(k) |
|---|---|
| 0.101 | 0.99944 ± 0.00003 |
| 0.510 | 0.9868 ± 0.0008 |
| 1.013 | 0.9638 ± 0.0020 |
| 2.002 | 0.9179 ± 0.0045 |
| 3.007 | 0.8698 ± 0.0065 |
| 3.698 | 0.8400 ± 0.0076 |
| 4.00 | 0.8284 ± 0.0079 |
| 5.00 | 0.7942 ± 0.0089 |
| 6.0 | 0.7680 ± 0.0095 |
| 7.01 | 0.7479 ± 0.0100 |
| 7.84 | 0.7356 |

This is 3.6 ± 0.2% suppression at k = 1 and 13.0 ± 0.7% at k = 3 h/Mpc.

**maxsupp_lowM (M_seed = 0.6).** Lowering the seed mass from 2.0 to 0.6 deepens the suppression:

| k (h/Mpc) | S(k) |
|---|---|
| 0.212 | 0.9967 |
| 0.510 | 0.9835 ± 0.0011 |
| 1.013 | 0.9557 ± 0.0029 |
| 2.002 | 0.9026 ± 0.0064 |
| 3.007 | 0.8521 ± 0.0094 |
| 3.698 | 0.8228 ± 0.0109 |

This is 4.4 ± 0.3% at k = 1 and 14.8 ± 0.9% at k = 3 h/Mpc, the largest suppression among the sampled points. It is not shown to be the maximum over the design range.

**maxsupp_lowkin (kinetic parameters at minimum).** This point shows essentially no suppression:

| k (h/Mpc) | S(k) |
|---|---|
| 0.212 | 1.0002 |
| 0.510 | 1.0004 ± 0.0007 |
| 1.013 | 1.0006 ± 0.0019 |
| 2.002 | 1.0033 ± 0.0042 |
| 3.007 | 0.9972 ± 0.0062 |
| 3.698 | 0.9883 ± 0.0071 |

In this emulator, v_kin and eps_kin therefore drive almost all the suppression up to k ≈ 3.7 h/Mpc, even with e_w at its maximum.

**fiducial versus strongAGN.** The S(k) values are:

| Point | k = 1.01 | k = 3.01 | k = 3.70 |
|---|---|---|---|
| fiducial | 0.9779 | 0.9197 | 0.8984 (std 0.004) |
| strongAGN | 0.9746 | 0.9121 | 0.8909 |

Raising the kinetic parameters and e_w at kappa_w = 3 therefore adds only about 0.3–0.8 percentage points of suppression over this range. These values come from an earlier run on this thread and were not independently re-verified in the present run.

**strongAGN beyond k = 3.7 h/Mpc.** S(k) continues to fall:

| k (h/Mpc) | S(k) |
|---|---|
| 5.25 | 0.851 |
| 7.01 | 0.8205 |
| 10.01 | 0.7946 (std 0.0098) |
| 12.55 | 0.7893 |

Between about 11.6 and 12.6 h/Mpc it flattens to a plateau of about 0.789–0.790, falling by less than 0.001 per 0.1 h/Mpc at the edge.

Two cautions apply to the high-k behaviour:

- The ratio has no upturn within the grid. The minimum is at or beyond k_max ≈ 12.6 h/Mpc, with a depth of about 21% for strongAGN.
- maxsupp is already at 0.7356 by k = 7.84, deeper than the strongAGN plateau. Its minimum is unresolved.

The k_max and plateau values come from byte offsets, and the final rows of the file were not quoted verbatim. They should be treated as approximate.

### Redshift evolution, z = 0 to z = 1

For maxsupp the suppression weakens strongly towards z = 1:

| k (h/Mpc) | S at z = 0 | S at z = 1 | Suppression, z = 0 to z = 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.013 | 0.9638 ± 0.0020 | 0.9781 ± 0.0018 | 3.6% to 2.2% |
| 3.007 | 0.8698 ± 0.0065 | 0.9299 ± 0.0055 | 13.0% to 7.0% |
| 3.70 | 0.8400 ± 0.0076 | 0.9214 ± 0.0064 | 16.0% to 7.9% |

Qualitatively, this matches the FLAMINGO statement that the response grows as z falls (arXiv:2410.17109). That comparison has not been checked against the FLAMINGO text. The ratio is still falling at k = 3.7 at both redshifts, so any shift of the minimum with redshift could not be measured.

[[FIGURE 28]]

Figure 28 plots the emulator Pk-ratio at z = 0 and z = 1 for the fiducial and maxsupp points. Only the maxsupp values in the table above were read out numerically. The fiducial z = 1 prediction was written but not read, so no quantitative z-trend is claimed for the fiducial point.

A planned companion plot of the four z = 0 variants was overwritten by this one, because the two plotting calls shared an output path.

### Gas fraction versus suppression

The fGas emulator gives M_gas/M500c inside R500c at z = 0 in three M500c bins: 5.01e13, 7.94e13 and 1.26e14 Msun/h.

| Point | f_gas at 1.26e14 Msun/h | f_gas at 7.94e13 Msun/h |
|---|---|---|
| fiducial | 0.1214 ± 0.0010 | 0.1090 |
| strongAGN | 0.1221 ± 0.0019 | 0.1098 |
| weakAGN | 0.1414 ± 0.0023 | 0.1375 |

Only fiducial and strongAGN have S(k) values to pair with these gas fractions. Their f_gas values agree within errors, with strongAGN nominally higher, yet strongAGN is 0.3–0.8 points more suppressed. This pair therefore shows no resolvable van Daalen-type relation (arXiv:1906.00968), and the nominal trend runs the wrong way.

The comparison has two weaknesses:

- It is confounded, because e_w changes together with the kinetic parameters.
- It is limited, because the weakAGN S(k) was never read. weakAGN has a markedly higher gas fraction, so it is the point that would make a three-point test meaningful.

One physical reading of the pair is that the emulator's suppression is driven by gas removed beyond R500c, or by haloes of other masses, rather than by the R500c gas fraction. This is untested.

### Comparison with observational suppression estimates

Errors are combined in quadrature, taking the published error on the side facing the emulator value. For maxsupp:

| Constraint | Gap |
|---|---|
| Grandis et al., k = 1 | 0.4 sigma (4.2% vs 3.6%) |
| Grandis et al., k = 3 | 1.7 sigma (18.4% vs 13.0%) |
| eROSITA + kSZ, k = 1 | 3.2 sigma short (10% vs 3.6%) |
| HSC-XXL, k = 1 | 0.35 sigma |

An earlier pass quoted about 3 and 8 sigma against Grandis et al. Those figures used emulator error alone and are superseded.

The strongest point, maxsupp_lowM, is:

- about 2.8 sigma short of eROSITA + kSZ;
- consistent with HSC-XXL and with Grandis et al. at k = 1;
- 3.6 points below Grandis et al. at k = 3.

All of these significances depend on literature values that have not been confirmed verbatim. They are also tested only at the kappa_w = 2, e_w = 1 corners with fixed cosmology.

### Weak-lensing impact (literature-based)

**Omega_m bias from ignoring or mis-modelling baryons.** Maraio, Hall and Taylor (arXiv:2410.12500, Table 3, read verbatim) consider an idealised Euclid-like Stage-IV cosmic-shear survey with ell_max = 5000:

| Ground truth | Model | 100 ΔΩ_m | Significance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Illustris | one-parameter HMCode, no theory error | −1.317 | −5.69 sigma |
| Illustris | same, with theoretical-error covariance | 0.128 | 0.249 sigma |
| Bahamas | one-parameter HMCode | 0.057 | 0.258 sigma |
| Eagle | six-parameter model, with theory error | 0.573 | 1.459 sigma |

The text adds two statements:

- The one-parameter model without theory error gives "at least a 3 sigma offset in either Omega_m or S8 for all hydro-sims excluding Bahamas".
- With Simba as ground truth, even ell_max = 1000 is biased by more than 2 sigma in all parameters.

The ΔS8 values are in that paper's Table 4, which was not read. This bias is therefore an Omega_m bias, not an S8 bias.

**Suppression needed to reconcile lensing with Planck.**

- For DES Y3, A_mod = 0.858 ± 0.052, with no scale cuts and a Planck prior (arXiv:2305.09827, Eq. 3). The suppression must extend to k ~ 0.2 h/Mpc.
- For KiDS-1000, A_mod ≈ 0.69 (arXiv:2206.11794).
- Without A_mod, DES Y3 S8 lies 0.9–1.8 sigma below Planck S8 = 0.828 ± 0.016, depending on analysis variant.

**Comparison with the emulator.** For maxsupp, S(k) is 0.9994 at k = 0.10 and 0.987 at k = 0.51 h/Mpc. The value at k ≈ 0.2 h/Mpc was not read but presumably lies below a 1% effect. For maxsupp_lowM the read value at k = 0.212 is 0.9967.

Emulator-level feedback therefore agrees with the Grandis et al. bound of less than 1% for k < 0.37 h/Mpc. It appears far weaker than A_mod = 0.86 or 0.69 would require at these scales. This is a qualitative comparison, because no A_mod-equivalent number was computed for any emulator point.

### Bibliographic and data products

Validated citation entries for arXiv:2305.09827, arXiv:2410.12500, arXiv:2512.02954 and arXiv:2309.02920, each with a verbatim abstract quote, were written to `runs/261023_143127/references.bib`.

Full texts of FLAMINGO (arXiv:2410.17109), Siegel et al. (arXiv:2512.02954) and Grandis et al. (arXiv:2309.02920) were downloaded to `runs/261023_143127/` as `.txt` files. They have not yet been read.

## Discussion

**Feedback physics in the emulator.** Within this emulator, the kinetic AGN mode is the lever on S(k). Switching it off removes almost all suppression even at maximum e_w. Lowering the seed mass, and plausibly lowering kappa_w (not isolated, because M_seed also changed), deepens it.

This is consistent with the general picture of AGN-driven gas expulsion from group-scale haloes. However, the emulator does not show the expected anti-correlation between the gas fraction inside R500c at about 1e14 Msun/h and the suppression. Possible reasons:

- the relevant gas is pushed beyond R500c;
- other halo masses dominate;
- the two-point comparison is simply too confounded to show it.

The literature (arXiv:1906.00968, arXiv:2509.04552, arXiv:2309.06479) predicts a clear relation, so this is a real tension worth resolving with the unread weakAGN curve and single-parameter sweeps.

**Size of the suppression.** The emulator's largest sampled suppression at k = 1 h/Mpc, 4.4%, agrees with HSC-XXL and Grandis et al. It falls short of the strong-feedback eROSITA + kSZ inference. At k = 3 h/Mpc it is below Grandis et al.

Three explanations are open:

- the design range may not span the strongest feedback now favoured observationally;
- the cosmology axes, untouched here, may shift the response through the baryon fraction and halo abundance;
- the P_grav reference may differ from P_DMO.

**Weak lensing.** The literature
